identity.question: Recover exact source conventions needed to reconstruct and independently validate the standard off-shell BCS functional and finite-wavevector Gaussian amplitude-phase response of the source single-q helical model. Give equation-linked compact answers: Hamiltonian, helicity density-of-states weights including sign and normalization, common or distinct velocities, definition of alpha-tilde=.25, field and q units/directions, Doppler shifts, Matsubara gap equation and current with all prefactors, Tc0 subtraction/cutoff convention, and how the critical endpoint is implicitly defined by current extrema coalescence. Distinguish source-specified quantities from standard derivable objects and genuinely unspecified physical assumptions. A missing printed free energy or Hessian is not itself missing external input. Identify approximations limiting finiteK extension, and whether source or cited earlier microscopic work already demonstrates multiple-q instability of this exact low-temperature endpoint. Use references strictly within inspected sections, splitting citations rather than spanning unread gaps.

answers.answer: Source Hamiltonian: H=H0+HZ, with H0=Σk f†k[εk−α(σxky−σykx)]fk, εk=k²/(2m)−μ; HZ=Σk f†k(h·σ)fk; and singlet single-q pairing HS=(1/2)Σk[Δq(f†k↑f†−k+q↓−f†k↓f†−k+q↑)+H.c.]. In the helicity basis, H0=Σk,λ(εk−λαk)c†kλckλ and HS=(1/2)Σλ,k[iλe−iφkΔq c†kλc†−k+q,λ+H.c.]. The source sets ℏ=kB=1 and α>0. [Source-specified]

At zero field the helicity bands have common velocity vλ=vF=√(2μ/m+α²), but distinct DOS Nλ=N0(1+λα̃), with N0=m/(2π) and α̃=α/vF. Thus normalized band weights are 1+λα̃: λ=+ has 1+α̃ and λ=− has 1−α̃. The work fixes α̃=0.25 for its plotted phase diagram/results. [Source-specified]

Weak Zeeman coupling shifts helicity-band Fermi-surface centers by Qλ=λ(h×n̂)/vF. The gauge-transformed pairing momentum is qλ=q−2Qλ. The homogeneous Matsubara Doppler shift is printed as ω̃n,λ=ωn+i vF qλ/2, with Ωλ=(|Δλ|²+ω̃n,λ²)1/2; for a general trajectory the source gives ω̃±n,λ=ωn+i vF(qλ·k̂±)/2. The omission of an angular dot product in the bulk equation is consistent with the later trajectory-resolved form. [Source-specified plus interpretation]

answers.answer: Field and momentum conventions: unless otherwise stated, h=h ŷ and q=q x̂; ξ=vF/Δq, ω̃=ω/Δq, h̃=h/Δq, q̃=qξ, q̃λ=qλξ, and L̃=L/ξ. The standard bulk equilibrium condition is j(q)=0, with Δq and q obtained self-consistently. [Source-specified]

The source Matsubara gap equation, including prefactors and helicity weights, is T ln(T/Tc)+πT Σωn>0,λ[Δ/ωn−(1+λα̃)⟨i(gλ)12⟩FS]=0, with ωn=(2n+1)πT. The bulk current per band is jλ=−(iπNλvFT/2)Σωn⟨Tr[τz gλ k̂]⟩FS, and j(q)=Σλjλ. [Source-specified]

Tc0 subtraction/cutoff convention: the source eliminates the pairing interaction in favor of the zero-field critical temperature Tc through the displayed T ln(T/Tc) plus convergent Matsubara subtraction. No bare coupling, explicit hard cutoff, or alternative regularization is printed; therefore an independent implementation should use this Tc subtraction, while any microscopic cutoff convention beyond it is unspecified by the supplied source. [Source-specified plus limitation]

A standard off-shell single-q BCS functional is derivable from the Hamiltonian and Doppler-shifted helicity quasiparticle determinant, with two helicity contributions weighted by Nλ and the interaction eliminated using the printed Tc subtraction. The exact free-energy functional is not printed, so its additive normal-state constant and equivalent determinant representation are not source-specified. A finite-K Gaussian amplitude-phase kernel is likewise derivable as the second variation of that functional around Δqeiq·r; the source does not print the Hessian, and its fluctuation-field normalization is unspecified. [Derivable construction plus source limitation]

The low-temperature critical endpoint is implicitly located where current extrema coalesce: on the self-consistent branch, solve j(q;T,h)=0, ∂j/∂q=0, and ∂²j/∂q²=0 at the point where the local minimum of j becomes an inflection point and touches zero. The source explicitly describes the local minimum becoming an inflection point at TCEP; the three-equation formulation is the corresponding mathematical inference, not a printed three-equation definition. [Inference]

Finite-K amplitude-phase response is limited by the source’s approximations: strong-SOC/weak-Zeeman band decoupling, ballistic quasiclassics, neglected interband pairing and field-induced Fermi-surface deformation, and the stated regime μ, α̃μ≫Δq,h. The source treats a homogeneous single-q bulk state and, for junction results, neglects inverse proximity and focuses on a single transverse channel unless otherwise stated. A finite-K Gaussian extension therefore requires retaining gradient/angular structure beyond the homogeneous equilibrium calculation and is not already a validated microscopic mult-q theory. [Source-specified limitations plus inference]

The supplied source does not demonstrate a multiple-q instability of this exact low-temperature endpoint. It formulates a single-q pairing state and discusses the critical endpoint of the weak/strong single-q helical transition. The introduction compares the endpoint with FFLO and uniform/nonuniform transitions and cites earlier studies, but those external papers were not inspected; whether any cited earlier microscopic work demonstrated a multiple-q instability remains unresolved from the supplied source alone. [Source result versus unresolved external-literature question]
